questions.question_english: Under which head of income should a government school teacher declare the remuneration received for evaluating CBSE board examination answer scripts (paid directly by CBSE, and not by their employer school)?
options_english: Income from Salaries
Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
Income from Other Sources
Income from Capital Gains
questions.explanation_english: For an amount to be taxable under the head 'Income from Salaries' (Section 15), there must exist an employer-employee (master-servant) relationship between the payer and the payee. When a government school teacher evaluates examination papers for an external examining body such as CBSE or acts as an invigilator/centre superintendent for CBSE/UPSC, CBSE is not the teacher's employer. Therefore, this remuneration/honorarium cannot be taxed under 'Salaries'. Since evaluation does not constitute carrying on a regular business or profession by the teacher, it is legally assessed under the residuary head 'Income from Other Sources' under Section 56 of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
questions.explanation_hindi: आयकर अधिनियम की धारा 15 के तहत 'वेतन' शीर्ष में किसी राशि के कराधान हेतु भुगतानकर्ता एवं प्राप्तकर्ता के मध्य नियोक्ता-कर्मचारी (मास्टर-सर्वेंट) का संबंध होना अनिवार्य है। जब कोई सरकारी शिक्षक CBSE या UPSC जैसी किसी बाहरी संस्था की बोर्ड परीक्षा उत्तर-पुस्तिकाओं के मूल्यांकन अथवा परीक्षा संचालन हेतु मानदेय प्राप्त करता है, तो शिक्षक और उस बोर्ड के बीच कोई नियोक्ता-कर्मचारी संबंध नहीं होता। अतः यह आय 'वेतन' या 'व्यवसाय/पेशा' में न आकर धारा 56 के अंतर्गत 'अन्य स्रोतों से आय' (Income from Other Sources) शीर्ष में कर-योग्य होती है।
questions.topic: Income Tax and GST Basics for School Administration
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Income from Other Sources

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Remuneration received for checking examination papers from an external agency like the Central Board of Secondary Education does not arise from an employer-employee relationship. Because there is no employer-employee relationship involved between the examiner and the external board, such earnings are legally assessed under the head Income from Other Sources.

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): An employee whose Form 26AS reflects less TDS than what was actually deducted as per their monthly salary pay slips can seamlessly claim the full tax credit while filing their Income Tax Return based solely on the pay slips.
Reason (R): Form 26AS is generated based on quarterly TDS returns filed by the employer; if the employer defaults in depositing the deducted tax or files the return with an incorrect PAN, the tax credit will not reflect in Form 26AS, resulting in an automated mismatch and demand notice from the CPC.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true. Under the automated e-filing and processing architecture of the Income Tax Department (CPC Bengaluru), tax credit claims in an Income Tax Return are strictly reconciled against the data pre-filled and validated in Form 26AS / Annual Information Statement (AIS). An employee cannot obtain tax credit merely on the strength of salary pay slips. If the employer or DDO fails to remit the tax into the government account or files Form 24Q with errors, the credit remains missing on TRACES, leading to an automated intimation/demand notice under Section 143(1). For the employee to obtain credit, the employer must rectify the discrepancy by filing a revised or correction TDS statement. Therefore, A is false and R is true.
questions.explanation_hindi: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है। आयकर विभाग के सेंट्रलाइज्ड प्रोसेसिंग सेंटर (CPC) की स्वचालित प्रणाली में आयकर रिटर्न में किए गए कर क्रेडिट दावों का मिलान अनिवार्य रूप से फॉर्म 26AS / AIS में दर्ज आंकड़ों से किया जाता है। कर्मचारी केवल वेतन पर्ची के आधार पर कर क्रेडिट प्राप्त नहीं कर सकता। यदि नियोक्ता या DDO कर जमा करने में विफल रहता है अथवा फॉर्म 24Q में गलत पैन दर्ज करता है, तो वह क्रेडिट TRACES पोर्टल पर प्रदर्शित नहीं होगा। ऐसी स्थिति में रिटर्न दाखिल करने पर धारा 143(1) के तहत क्रेडिट बेमेल (mismatch) का नोटिस और कर मांग जारी हो जाएगी। क्रेडिट प्राप्त करने के लिए नियोक्ता को संशोधित टीडीएस रिटर्न (correction statement) दाखिल करना अनिवार्य होता है। अतः A गलत है और R सही है।
questions.topic: Income Tax and GST Basics for School Administration
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) A is false but R is true

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: If Form 26AS reflects less TDS than shown on salary pay slips due to employer default or non- filing, the employee cannot claim tax credit based solely on pay slips. Tax credits are processed strictly based on Form 26AS entries, resulting in potential demand notices until the employer files corrected returns.

questions.question_english: A school DDO realizes on 5th June that they forgot to file the Q4 (January–March) quarterly TDS return, which was statutorily due on 31st May. What is the statutory late filing fee applicable under Section 234E of the Income Tax Act?
options_english: ₹100 for every single day during which the failure continues, without any upper ceiling limit.
₹200 per day of failure, subject to a maximum cap equal to the total TDS deductible for that quarter.
A flat statutory penalty of ₹5,000 regardless of the duration of delay.
1% of the total TDS amount per day of delay.
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 234E of the Income Tax Act, 1961, where a person fails to deliver or cause to be delivered a statement of TDS (such as Form 24Q or Form 26Q) within the prescribed due date, they are liable to pay a mandatory fee of ₹200 for every day during which the failure continues. However, Section 234E(2) specifies an important statutory limitation: the total late fee payable shall not exceed the total amount of tax deductible/collectible for that particular quarter. This fee is mandatory and is computed automatically by TRACES/CPC-TDS before the return can be processed.
questions.explanation_hindi: आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 234E के अनुसार, यदि कोई कटौतीकर्ता/डीडीओ निर्धारित समय-सीमा (जैसे Q4 के लिए 31 मई) के भीतर टीडीएस विवरणी (Form 24Q/26Q) दाखिल करने में विफल रहता है, तो उसे चूक जारी रहने तक ₹200 प्रतिदिन की दर से अनिवार्य विलंब शुल्क देना होता है। धारा 234E(2) के तहत यह स्पष्ट सीमा निर्धारित है कि संचित विलंब शुल्क की कुल राशि उस तिमाही के कुल कटौती योग्य टीडीएस (TDS) से अधिक नहीं हो सकती। यह राशि रिटर्न दाखिल करने से पूर्व चालान द्वारा जमा की जाती है।
questions.topic: Income Tax and GST Basics for School Administration
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) ₹200 per day of failure, capped at total TDS amount.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: amount. Under Section 234E of the Income Tax Act, delay in filing a quarterly TDS return attracts a mandatory late fee of two hundred rupees for every single day during which the compliance failure continues. The total fee accumulated cannot exceed the total amount of tax deductible for that specific quarter.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the remittance and filing of TDS by Government Offices:
I. Government deductors are permitted to remit deducted TDS to the credit of the Central Government without the production of an income-tax challan through a Book Adjustment.
II. When TDS is remitted via Book Adjustment, the concerned Pay and Accounts Officer (PAO) or Treasury Officer must file Form 24G to the agency authorized by the DGIT (Systems).
III. Government offices and educational institutions are exempt from filing quarterly TDS returns.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II, and III
questions.explanation_english:
Statement I is correct: Under Rule 30(1) of the Income Tax Rules, where tax has been deducted by or on behalf of the Government, it may be remitted to the credit of the Central Government on the same day through book adjustment (transfer entry) without producing an ITNS 281 challan.
Statement II is correct: Under Section 200(2A) and Rule 31A(1)(a), whenever tax is credited to the Central Government by book adjustment without challan, the PAO, Treasury Officer, or designated accounting authority must file a monthly statement in Form 24G by the 10th of the following month (or 30th April for March). This generates a Book Identification Number (BIN) for each DDO.
Statement III is incorrect: Government offices are NOT exempt from filing quarterly TDS returns. The school DDO is statutorily mandated to file Form 24Q/26Q every quarter, quoting the Book Identification Number (BIN) received from the PAO/Treasury in place of the bank challan BSR code and CIN.
Thus, only Statements I and II are correct.
questions.explanation_hindi:
कथन I सही है: आयकर नियम, 1962 के नियम 30(1) के अनुसार, सरकारी विभागों एवं कार्यालयों द्वारा काटा गया टीडीएस बिना किसी बैंक चालान (ITNS 281) के सीधे बही समायोजन (Book Adjustment/Transfer Voucher) द्वारा उसी दिन केंद्र सरकार के खाते में जमा कराया जा सकता है।
कथन II सही है: आयकर अधिनियम की धारा 200(2A) तथा नियम 31A के तहत, बुक एडजस्टमेंट से कर जमा होने पर संबंधित वेतन एवं लेखा अधिकारी (PAO) या कोषागार अधिकारी को प्रत्येक माह की 10 तारीख तक 'फॉर्म 24G' दाखिल करना होता है, जिससे संबंधित डीडीओ के लिए बुक आइडेंटिफिकेशन नंबर (BIN) जनरेट होता है।
कथन III गलत है: किसी भी सरकारी कार्यालय या विद्यालय को त्रैमासिक टीडीएस रिटर्न (Form 24Q/26Q) दाखिल करने से कोई छूट प्राप्त नहीं है; डीडीओ को बैंक चालान के स्थान पर कोषागार से प्राप्त BIN का उपयोग करते हुए अनिवार्य रूप से त्रैमासिक रिटर्न दाखिल करना होता है।
अतः केवल कथन I और II सही हैं।
questions.topic: Income Tax and GST Basics for School Administration
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I and II only

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Government deductors can remit tax deducted at source to the government treasury without using traditional income tax challans via Book Adjustment entries. In such cases, the Treasury Officer or Pay and Accounts Officer must file Form 24G. However, government offices are not exempt from filing mandatory quarterly TDS returns.

questions.question_english: A government school teacher deposits ₹50,000 into their Tier-II National Pension System (NPS) account. Can this contribution be claimed as a tax deduction under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act, 1961?
options_english: Yes, all Tier-II NPS contributions are unconditionally eligible under Section 80C.
Yes, provided the teacher does not simultaneously claim any PPF investment deduction.
No, Tier-II NPS contributions are not eligible under Section 80C for state government employees.
Yes, but it can only be claimed under Section 80CCD(1B) up to ₹50,000.
questions.explanation_english: Contributions made into a Tier-II NPS account represent voluntary, non-locked savings that can be withdrawn at any time, and generally do not qualify for any tax deductions. Under Section 80C(2)(xxv) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 (introduced via the NPS Tier-II Tax Saver Scheme, 2020), deduction under Section 80C is strictly restricted to Central Government employees who contribute to a designated Tier-II account with a mandatory 3-year lock-in period. State government employees and private subscribers are not eligible for this deduction. Furthermore, Section 80CCD(1B) provides an exclusive deduction of up to ₹50,000 only for contributions to Tier-I NPS accounts, not Tier-II accounts.
questions.explanation_hindi: NPS टीयर-II खाता एक स्वैच्छिक बचत खाता (withdrawal-friendly facility) है जिसमें जमा राशि पर सामान्यतः कोई कर छूट नहीं मिलती। आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 80C(2)(xxv) के तहत 'NPS Tier-II Tax Saver Scheme 2020' के माध्यम से धारा 80C की कटौती केवल केंद्र सरकार के कर्मचारियों को 3 वर्ष की अनिवार्य लॉक-इन अवधि के साथ प्रदान की जाती है। राज्य सरकार के कर्मचारियों अथवा अन्य अंशदाताओं के लिए टीयर-II अंशदान धारा 80C के तहत पात्र नहीं है। इसके अतिरिक्त, धारा 80CCD(1B) के तहत ₹50,000 की विशेष कटौती केवल टीयर-I खाते के लिए अनुमन्य है, टीयर-II के लिए नहीं। अतः विकल्प C सही उत्तर है।
questions.topic: Income Tax and GST Basics for School Administration
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) No, Tier-II NPS contributions are not eligible under 80C for state employees.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: eligible under 80C for state employees. Contributions made into a Tier-II National Pension System account are voluntary savings that do not qualify for tax deductions under Section 80C for state government employees. questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding Input Tax Credit (ITC) for government and recognized schools:
I. Since the primary educational services provided by schools are exempt from GST, schools generally cannot claim ITC on the goods and services they purchase.
II. The GST paid on the purchase of computers for a computer lab by a school becomes a cost to the school as ITC is blocked under Section 17(2).

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 17(2) of the CGST Act, 2017, where goods or services are used by a registered person partly for effecting taxable supplies and partly for effecting exempt supplies, the amount of credit is restricted to so much of the input tax as is attributable to taxable supplies. Because schools supply exempt educational services (under Entry 66 of Notification No. 12/2017), they are not entitled to avail ITC on their purchases. Consequently, GST paid on computer hardware, science lab apparatus, furniture, or stationery is an outright non-recoverable expense (cost) to the school (Statements I and II are correct). Statement III is incorrect: the GST Council is a constitutional recommendatory body, not a tax-refund disbursing authority, and GST law does not permit any refund of input taxes incurred on capital goods or works contracts used for exempt educational supplies.
questions.explanation_hindi: CGST अधिनियम, 2017 की धारा 17(2) के अनुसार, यदि खरीदी गई वस्तुओं या सेवाओं का उपयोग कर-मुक्त आपूर्ति (Exempt Supplies) के लिए किया जाता है, तो उस पर इनपुट टैक्स क्रेडिट (ITC) प्राप्त नहीं किया जा सकता। चूँकि स्कूल मुख्य रूप से कर-मुक्त शैक्षणिक सेवाएँ देते हैं, अतः वे कंप्यूटर, लैब उपकरण, फर्नीचर या स्टेशनरी की खरीद पर चुकाए गए जीएसटी का क्रेडिट नहीं ले सकते। इसलिए चुकाया गया जीएसटी स्कूल के लिए शुद्ध अतिरिक्त खर्च बन जाता है (कथन I और II सही हैं)। कथन III गलत है क्योंकि जीएसटी परिषद कोई रिफंड प्राधिकरण नहीं है और कर-मुक्त सेवाओं हेतु खरीदे गए बुनियादी सामान पर जीएसटी रिफंड का कोई कानूनी प्रावधान नहीं है।

questions.explanation_english:
The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced in India through the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016, which received Presidential assent on September 8, 2016 and came into full legal effect on July 1, 2017.
Key constitutional provisions introduced by this amendment include:
- Article 246A: Conferred concurrent powers on Parliament and State Legislatures to make laws with respect to goods and services tax.
- Article 269A: Provided for the levy and collection of GST on inter-state supply and imports by the Government of India, to be apportioned between the Union and the States.
- Article 279A: Established the Goods and Services Tax Council (GST Council) chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
(Note: The 100th Amendment dealt with the Land Boundary Agreement with Bangladesh; the 73rd introduced Panchayati Raj in 1992; and the 105th restored state governments' power to identify Socially and Educationally Backward Classes).

भारत में वस्तु एवं सेवा कर (GST) को 'संविधान (एक सौ एकवाँ संशोधन) अधिनियम, 2016' के माध्यम से लागू किया गया, जिसे 8 सितंबर 2016 को राष्ट्रपति की स्वीकृति प्राप्त हुई तथा 1 जुलाई 2017 से राष्ट्रव्यापी रूप से प्रभावी किया गया।
इस संशोधन द्वारा किए गए प्रमुख संवैधानिक परिवर्तन:
- अनुच्छेद 246A: संसद और राज्य विधानसभाओं को वस्तु एवं सेवा कर लगाने हेतु समवर्ती विधायी शक्तियां प्रदान की गईं।

questions.question_english: In a situation where the Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) has deducted TDS from an employee's salary but fails to deposit it into the Central Government account, what statutory protection is available to the employee under the Income Tax Act, 1961?
options_english: The employee is legally required to pay the tax amount once again directly to the Income Tax Department

questions.explanation_english: Section 205 of the Income Tax Act, 1961 provides express statutory protection to taxpayers from whom tax has already been withheld at source. It states that where tax is deductible at source, the assessee (employee) shall not be called upon to pay the tax himself to the extent to which tax has actually been deducted from that income. The CBDT, through Office Memorandums and instructions (e.g., Instruction No. 275/29/2014-IT(B)), as well as several landmark High Court judgments, has reiterated that the tax recovery proceedings for deducted but unremitted TDS can only be instituted against the defaulting deductor/employer as an 'assessee-in-default' under Section 201, and cannot be recovered from the employee whose tax was deducted at source.
questions.explanation_hindi: आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 205 करदाता (कर्मचारी) को स्पष्ट सांविधिक संरक्षण प्रदान करती है। धारा 205 के अनुसार, जहां किसी आय से स्रोत पर कर की कटौती कर ली गई है, उस सीमा तक संबंधित करदाता से दोबारा कर भुगतान की मांग नहीं की जा सकती। सीबीडीटी (CBDT) के निर्देशों (जैसे अनुदेश सं. 275/29/2014-IT(B)) और विभिन्न उच्च न्यायालयों के न्यायिक निर्णयों में यह स्पष्ट किया गया है कि यदि नियोक्ता/DDO ने वेतन से कर काट लिया है और उसे सरकारी खजाने में जमा नहीं किया है, तो आयकर विभाग कर्मचारी से उस कर की वसूली नहीं कर सकता। विभाग धारा 201 के अंतर्गत दोषी कटौतीकर्ता (DDO) को ही 'डिफ़ॉल्ट में निर्धारिती' मानते हुए ब्याज और जुर्माने सहित वसूली की कार्यवाही करने के लिए बाध्य है। अतः विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।

questions.question_english: A new Principal assumes charge of a government school following the transfer of the previous Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO). With respect to the Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number (TAN) required for filing TDS returns for the school, what should the new Principal do?
options_english: Apply immediately for a new TAN in their personal name for future school tax deductions.
Continue using the school's existing TAN allotted to the office/post of the DDO.
Use their personal PAN instead of TAN to ensure individual accountability.
Request the previous DDO to continue filing the school's returns from their new posting.
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 203A of the Income Tax Act, 1961, every person deducting or collecting tax at source must apply for and quote a Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number (TAN). In the case of government offices, schools, and institutions, the TAN is allotted to the drawing and disbursing office/post (e.g., Principal/DDO of the school) rather than to an individual officer in their personal capacity. Consequently, whenever there is an administrative transfer, retirement, or change in incumbency, the successor DDO must continue to utilize the existing permanent TAN already allotted to that office for all tax deductions, challan payments (ITNS 281), and quarterly return filings (Form 24Q/26Q). Applying for multiple TANs for the same deductor office is prohibited and invites penalty under Section 272BB.
questions.explanation_hindi: आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 203A के अनुसार, स्रोत पर कर कटौती (TDS) करने वाले प्रत्येक व्यक्ति या कार्यालय के लिए कर कटौती एवं संग्रहण खाता संख्या (TAN) प्राप्त करना और उद्धृत करना अनिवार्य है। सरकारी विद्यालयों या कार्यालयों में टैन (TAN) किसी अधिकारी विशेष के व्यक्तिगत नाम पर नहीं, बल्कि उस कार्यालय के आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) के पद के नाम पर आवंटित होता है। इसलिए, जब पूर्व प्रधानाचार्य/डीडीओ का स्थानांतरण होता है, तो कार्यभार ग्रहण करने वाले नए प्रधानाचार्य को विद्यालय के उसी पूर्व-आवंटित स्थायी टैन (TAN) का उपयोग जारी रखना चाहिए। एक ही कार्यालय के लिए दूसरा टैन लेना न केवल अनावश्यक है, बल्कि आयकर नियमों के तहत प्रतिबंधित भी है।

questions.question_english:
Consider the following sequence of events regarding a Drawing and Disbursing Officer's (DDO) responsibilities and an employee's rights:
I. An employee fails or refuses to submit Form 12BB and investment proofs within the timeline set by the school.
II. The DDO calculates TDS under Section 192 without granting unverified deductions and deducts tax accordingly.
III. The employee later files their personal Income Tax Return (ITR) with the Income Tax Department and claims deductions based on actual eligible investments, seeking a refund.
Is the above sequence legally valid and acceptable under Income Tax rules?
options_english: No, the DDO commits an offense by deducting excess tax without considering eligible deductions.
No, employees are legally barred from claiming deductions in their ITR if omitted from employer declarations.
Yes, the DDO is legally protected and the employee can claim eligible deductions and refund in their personal ITR.
Yes, but the DDO must report the unverified investment claims in Part B of Form 16.
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 192 read with Rule 26C of the Income Tax Rules, 1962, a DDO is legally prohibited from allowing tax deductions without having received Form 12BB along with substantiated documentary proof. If an employee fails to submit proofs within the stipulated deadline, the DDO is legally bound to compute TDS on the basis of available records without allowing unverified deductions. This procedure protects the DDO from penalties for short deduction under Section 201. Simultaneously, the employee does not forfeit their statutory rights; under Section 139 and Section 237, the employee can claim all bona fide Chapter VI-A deductions while filing their personal ITR and receive a refund of excess TDS deducted directly from the Income Tax Department.
questions.explanation_hindi: आयकर अधिनियम की धारा 192 और नियम 26C के तहत DDO केवल उन्हीं कटौतियों को स्वीकार कर सकता है जिनके लिए कर्मचारी ने फॉर्म 12BB और दस्तावेजी साक्ष्य प्रस्तुत किए हों। साक्ष्य न मिलने पर DDO बिना कटौती के TDS काटने के लिए विधिक रूप से बाध्य है और धारा 201 के तहत किसी भी शास्ति से सुरक्षित रहता है। वहीं दूसरी ओर, कर्मचारी के वैधानिक अधिकार समाप्त नहीं होते हैं; धारा 139 के तहत अपना व्यक्तिगत आयकर रिटर्न (ITR) भरते समय वह अपने सभी वैध निवेशों का दावा कर सकता है तथा धारा 237 के तहत अधिक कटे हुए कर का रिफंड सीधे आयकर विभाग से प्राप्त कर सकता है। अतः विकल्प C सही उत्तर है।

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Admission fees, tuition fees, and examination fees collected by a recognized government school from its students are exempt from GST.
Reason (R): Under statutory GST notifications, services provided by an educational institution offering education up to higher secondary school to its students are categorized as an exempt supply.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation_english: Assertion (A) is correct: Core educational charges including admission fees, tuition fees, laboratory fees, and examination fees collected directly from enrolled students by recognized schools are completely exempt from GST. Reason (R) is also correct: Under Entry 66(a) of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), services provided by an educational institution to its students, faculty, and staff are specifically declared as exempt supplies. Because the primary educational service is exempt, all statutory educational fees that are naturally bundled as part of schooling qualify for exemption. Therefore, Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A).
questions.explanation_hindi: अभिकथन (A) सही है: मान्यता प्राप्त सरकारी या निजी स्कूलों द्वारा अपने छात्रों से लिया जाने वाला प्रवेश शुल्क, शिक्षण शुल्क (ट्यूशन फीस) और परीक्षा शुल्क पूरी तरह से जीएसटी से मुक्त (Exempt) है। कारण (R) भी सही है: अधिसूचना संख्या 12/2017-केंद्रीय कर (दर) की प्रविष्टि 66(a) के अनुसार, पूर्व-प्राथमिक से उच्चतर माध्यमिक स्तर तक के शैक्षणिक संस्थानों द्वारा अपने छात्रों को दी जाने वाली सेवाएँ कर-मुक्त आपूर्ति हैं। चूँकि मुख्य विद्यालयीन शिक्षा कर-मुक्त है, इसलिए स्कूल द्वारा छात्रों से ली जाने वाली ये सभी शैक्षणिक फीस भी कर-मुक्त होती हैं। अतः (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या है।

Assertion (A): DDOs are legally empowered to grant relief under Section 89(1) while calculating TDS on arrears of salary.
Reason (R): The employee must furnish particulars of such arrears in Form 10E to the employer/tax portal to enable the DDO to allow the relief.

questions.explanation_english: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A). Under Section 192(2A) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, a Drawing and Disbursing Officer is legally authorized to compute and allow relief under Section 89(1) while estimating TDS on salary arrears paid to government or semi-government employees. However, a mandatory statutory condition is that the employee must compute the relief under Rule 21A and electronically furnish the particulars in Form 10E on the e-filing portal of the Income Tax Department and submit the acknowledgment to the DDO. Without Form 10E, the DDO cannot legally grant the relief.

Consider the following statements regarding the Goods and Services Tax (GST) framework in India:
I. GST is a destination-based consumption tax.
II. The input tax credit (ITC) chain is deliberately broken between the manufacturer and the retailer under GST.
III. Integrated GST (IGST) is levied and collected by the Central Government on inter-state supplies and imports.
IV. Alcoholic liquor for human consumption is completely subsumed under the GST framework.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I and III only

questions.explanation_english:
An analysis of each statement reveals:
- Statement I is correct: GST is a multi-stage, destination-based consumption tax, meaning the tax revenue ultimately accrues to the jurisdiction where the consumption of goods or services occurs.
- Statement II is incorrect: The primary objective of GST is to ensure an unbroken, seamless chain of Input Tax Credit (ITC) from the raw material manufacturer down to the final retailer, eliminating the cascading effect of taxes ('tax on tax').
- Statement III is correct: Under Article 269A of the Constitution and Section 5 of the IGST Act, 2017, IGST is levied and collected by the Central Government on all inter-state supplies of goods and services and on imports into India.
- Statement IV is incorrect: Alcoholic liquor for human consumption is constitutionally excluded from the definition of GST under Article 366(12A) and continues to be taxed under State Excise Duty and State VAT.
Therefore, only statements I and III are correct.
questions.explanation_hindi:
कथनों का विस्तृत विश्लेषण:
- कथन I सही है: जीएसटी एक बहु-स्तरीय, गंतव्य-आधारित उपभोग कर है। इसका तात्पर्य यह है कि कर का राजस्व उस राज्य या क्षेत्राधिकार को प्राप्त होता है जहाँ वस्तुओं या सेवाओं का अंतिम उपभोग होता है।
- कथन II गलत है: जीएसटी का मुख्य उद्देश्य विनिर्माता से लेकर अंतिम खुदरा विक्रेता तक इनपुट टैक्स क्रेडिट (ITC) की एक निर्बाध और निरंतर श्रृंखला प्रदान करना है, जिससे कर-पर-कर (कैस्केडिंग प्रभाव) पूरी तरह समाप्त हो जाता है।
- कथन III सही है: संविधान के अनुच्छेद 269A तथा IGST अधिनियम, 2017 की धारा 5 के अंतर्गत, अंतर-राज्यीय आपूर्ति तथा भारत में होने वाले आयातों पर केंद्र सरकार द्वारा एकीकृत जीएसटी (IGST) लगाया और वसूला जाता है।
- कथन IV गलत है: संविधान के अनुच्छेद 366(12A) के तहत मानव उपभोग हेतु मादक शराब को जीएसटी की परिभाषा से बाहर रखा गया है। इस पर आज भी राज्य उत्पाद शुल्क और वैट (VAT) लागू हैं।
अतः केवल कथन I और III सही हैं।
